native_profile: Linux x86_64 GCC C++17 -O2 against the pinned modeling library
verified_cases: constructor rejection and protected-init acceptance of equal zero weights
dimension-changing weighted init, rationality recomputation, resolution cache invalidation, and evaluation representation clearing
null weight pointer resets rationality and clears evaluation representation
same-total-size but mismatched 3x2 and 2x3 arrays raise Standard_DimensionMismatch after pole replacement, retaining prior rational flags, cached resolution and representation
native_failure_domain: Run `/tmp/tkg3d_bezier_surface_init_probe same-count-crash` after compiling the probe. It prints `before-same-count-init` and exits by SIGSEGV (shell status 139) when a nonrational 2x2 surface is reinitialized with same-size rational weights. Equivalent 2D and 3D Bezier curve probes also crash; see porting/audits/bezier-curve-protected-init.json. Rust safely completes these calls, so this input sequence remains an explicit behavior divergence.
limitations: Post-exception resized weight cells are not read because OCCT leaves them uninitialized.
The native crash is recorded as an observed upstream failure, not emulated as a Rust process crash.
This does not establish complete TKG3d API or cross-platform parity.
